May 6 recap: Northwest Indiana news you may have missed today
Don't miss Wednesday's most popular stories from The Times.
(10) updates to this series since
Travis d'Arnaud hit a three-run home run to highlight a five-run second inning and Walbert Urena allowed one run on two hits to help the Angels beat the White Sox.
Powers Health is investing $80 million in a new five-story medical building on the Community Hospital campus in Munster.
Former Gary Deputy Police Chief James Bond will be released on $20,000 bond ahead of his federal trial on sexual exploitation charges.
"The only place that can be entertained is probably way before your primary, and, of course, ours has passed," said Indiana Gov. Mike Braun.
A suspect was arrested after police asked for the public's help in identifying a person of interest connected to a burglary incident that occurred late last month.
The Chicago Sky's 2025 first-round pick won't play for the team this season. Instead, she'll go to college.
An 18-year-old Bloomington man is jailed on charges that he fired a handgun into a crowd during Little 500 revelry on Kirkwood Avenue on April 26, injuring two women with bullet fragments.
The Blackhawks will pick fourth in the NHL draft, their fourth consecutive year with a top-four pick. Chicago entered Tuesday’s lottery with the second-highest odds of landing the top pick.
Gasoline sold in Indiana should cost about 60 cents a gallon less than other states after Gov. Mike Braun suspended all state taxes on gasoline purchases.
An area resident was injured while trying to extinguish a fire at home with a blanket designed for that purpose, officials said.
